Brings the repo into alignment with Snyk ProdSec standards: [GitHub Repository Setup Standard](https://snyksec.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODSEC/pages/3626238021), [Secure Configuration Standard](https://snyksec.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODSEC/pages/3626926083), and [CLA for Public Repositories](https://snyksec.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODSEC/pages/3978526730).

**In-repo changes**
- **catalog-info.yaml** — Backstage asset classification (`external-tooling`, owner `probely-frontend`) for the software catalog.
- **.github/workflows/security.yml** — Security scanning workflow: Snyk Open Source (SCA), Snyk Code (SAST), and secret detection via `probely/snyk-prodsec` reusable workflow (push/PR to `main`, weekly schedule, `workflow_dispatch`).
- **.github/workflows/cla.yml** — CLA Assistant workflow for contributor license agreement checks (Snyk OSS gist).
- **.github/pull_request_template.md** — Breaking changes section, documentation checklist, simplified testing to "CI checks pass", Snyk scan item in security considerations.
- **prompts.md** — Example prompts for parallel target onboarding (taintedport.com, screaming-goat.netlify.app, umuv.world/muvents).

**GitHub settings (applied via API)**
- Branch protection on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code owner review, status checks (test + lint), branches up to date, signed commits, no bypass, no force push.
- Repo settings: Issues/Projects/Wiki disabled where applicable, GitHub Pages off, auto-delete head branches on merge, merge commits disallowed (squash/rebase only).

## Summary

- The tool handler maintains feature parity with CLI commands while adapting output format for tool consumption
- Tool mode instructions use JSON-style syntax to match the tool's actual interface

author: jperezdelreal
body:
Closes the mobile portrait UX issue.

## Problem
The game forced landscape orientation on mobile, but the maze is **vertical** (28×31 tiles = 672×744px). Portrait is the natural orientation.

## Changes
- **Removed** the landscape orientation warning overlay (CSS + JS)
- **Added** portrait-aware canvas scaling using \calc(100dvh - 240px)\ (with \h\ fallback) so the entire game canvas fits above the D-pad controls
- **D-pad controls** remain visible at the bottom without overlapping the canvas
- Works on standard phones: iPhone 14 (390×844), iPhone SE (375×667), Android (360×800)

## Technical Details
- Canvas \max-height\ constrains the display size in portrait while \width: auto\ preserves aspect ratio
- Uses \dvh\ (dynamic viewport height) for accurate mobile sizing, with \h\ fallback
- \setupOrientationWarning()\ is now a no-op to avoid breaking the existing constructor call chain

author: dunkelheit
body:
## Summary

 Bundles three related housekeeping improvements that round out the repository's community health setup:

 1. TypeScript fix — the neverSettles spy in the maxSize eviction test was typed as () => Promise<string> (no parameters). Because recycle infers TArgs from the wrapped function, the returned recyclableFunc
 was also typed as taking zero arguments, causing a "Expected 0 arguments, but got 1" error in VSCode whenever the test called recyclableFunc('key-1'). The spy signature is changed to (..._args: unknown[])
 => Promise<string> so the type correctly reflects that the function can receive arguments (passed by the custom keyBuilder) even if it does not use them.
 2. ESLint rule — the _-prefix convention for intentionally unused identifiers is now formally configured in eslint.config.js via @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars with argsIgnorePattern, varsIgnorePattern,
 and caughtErrorsIgnorePattern all set to '^_'. Without this, the linter would flag the _args parameter introduced by the fix above.
 3. Community health files — CONTRIBUTING.md is moved from .github/ to the repository root (GitHub surfaces it more prominently there), and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 3.0) is added.

author: toddgrun
body: Perf numbers came back and weren't great -- no improvement. Looks like the call to AbsoluteUri moved to GetHashCode, and I'm not seeing a way to make that work given what the comments in that method indicate. Going to close this out as I'm not seeing a path forward with it -- you win some, you lose some. *** Original Description *** Previously, the ctor taking in a Uri called Uri.AbsoluteUri to populate the UriString property. This shows as about 0.4% of all allocations in devenv in the TypingInWebforms ddrit test. Instead, the ctor taking in a Uri will no longer set the field backing the UriString property, instead setting that field on demand when the UriString property is called. This optimization only helps if a large number of DocumentUri instances are constructed but don't invoke the UriString property. Debugging through this, I see the vast majority of calls to the UriString property come through the Equals implementation. If we have _parsedUri fields, then we can short-circuit before calling the UriString property by checking the OriginalString of each parsed uri. In my testing, these are almost always equal, thus avoiding the call to UriString and the corresponding allocations. *** Before allocations *** ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/82763)

## Summary

Adds auto-refresh polling to all three ticket status pages so users see live updates without manual reloads.

## Changes

### New files
- `src/hooks/use-auto-refresh.ts` — shared polling hook with configurable interval and automatic cleanup on unmount
- `src/components/last-updated.tsx` — subtle "Updated X ago" indicator with spinning refresh icon during polls

### Updated pages

| Page | Interval | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|
| Dashboard ticket list | 30s | Silent background refresh, no loading flash |
| Dashboard ticket detail | 20s | Skips poll if status change is in flight |
| Public ticket detail | 20s | Converted from server → client component |

### API update
- `GET /api/tickets/[publicId]` now returns `screenshots` field (needed for client-side public page)

## Behaviour
- **No loading spinner on background refresh** — avoids UI flicker, stale data stays visible until new data arrives
- **Interval cleanup on unmount** — no memory leaks
- **Resilient** — silent poll failures are swallowed; users keep seeing their last good data
- **Poll pause during edits** — detail page skips refresh while a status update PATCH is in-flight

author: copilot
body:
PaaS platforms like Railway only allow mounting a single volume, making the existing multi-mount Docker Compose layout (`./forms:/app/forms`, `./logo.png:/app/static/logo.png`, etc.) unusable there.

## Solution

New optional `APP_DATA_DIR` env var that redirects all user-provided inputs to a single directory. When unset, behavior is **identical to today** — `docker-compose.yml` is untouched.

### Expected volume layout when `APP_DATA_DIR=/data`:
```
/data/
├── forms/           ← YAML form definitions
├── pdf_templates/   ← optional custom PDF templates
└── logo.png         ← optional logo (per APP_COMPANY__LOGO_FILENAME)
```

## Changes

- **`config.py`** — `data_dir: Optional[str] = None` added to `AppSettings` (env: `APP_DATA_DIR`)
- **`factory.py`** — When `data_dir` is set: resolves `forms_dir` and `pdf_templates_dir` from it; copies logo into `app.static_folder` at startup with error logging
- **`form_engine.py`** — `FormEngine.__init__` gains `pdf_templates_dir: Optional[str] = None`, forwarded to `PdfGenerator`
- **`Dockerfile`** — Pre-creates `/data/forms` and `/data/pdf_templates` as mount-point stubs
- **`README.md`** — Railway/PaaS deployment section added

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Problem

Railway App (and similar PaaS platforms) only allows mounting **a single volume**. The current deployment model relies on multiple separate volume mounts (`./forms:/app/forms`, `./pdf_templates:/app/pdf_templates`, `./logo.png:/app/static/logo.png`, etc.), which works perfectly for On-Prem Docker Compose but is incompatible with Railway's single-volume constraint.

Additionally, mounting a volume at `/app` on Railway overwrites all app files (including `static/`, `src/`, etc.), breaking the application entirely.

## Solution: `APP_DATA_DIR` environment variable

Introduce a new optional environment variable `APP_DATA_DIR` that, when set, tells the app to look for user-provided data files (forms, logo) in that directory. This allows mounting a single volume (e.g., `/data`) that contains everything the user needs to customize.

### Expected directory structure when `APP_DATA_DIR` is set:

```
$APP_DATA_DIR/           (e.g., /data)
├── forms/               ← YAML form definitions
├── pdf_templates/       ← optional custom PDF templates  
└── logo.png             ← optional company logo (or whatever APP_COMPANY__LOGO_FILENAME is set to)
```

### Behavior

**When `APP_DATA_DIR` is set** (e.g., `APP_DATA_DIR=/data` on Railway):
1. Load form YAML files from `$APP_DATA_DIR/forms/` instead of `/app/forms/`
2. Load PDF templates from `$APP_DATA_DIR/pdf_templates/` instead of `/app/pdf_templates/` (if the directory exists there)
3. At startup, copy the logo file from `$APP_DATA_DIR/<logo_filename>` to `/app/static/<logo_filename>` (if it exists), so Flask can serve it from its static folder
4. Continue storing generated PDFs in `/app/pdfs/` and drafts in `/app/drafts/` (these are ephemeral/output data, not user-provided input)

**When `APP_DATA_DIR` is NOT set** (On-Prem Docker Compose):
- Everything works exactly as before — no behavioral change whatsoever
- The existing `docker-compose.yml` with its individual volume mounts remains fully functional

### Files to modify

1. **`src/formflow/config.py`** — Add `data_dir: Optional[str] = None` field to `AppSettings` (env var: `APP_DATA_DIR`)

2. **`src/formflow/factory.py`** — In `create_app()`:
   - After loading settings, check if `data_dir` is set
   - If set, copy logo from `$APP_DATA_DIR/<logo_filename>` → `/app/static/<logo_filename>` (if the file exists)
   - Pass the resolved `forms_dir` to `FormEngine`
   - Pass the resolved `pdf_templates_dir` to `PdfGenerator` (if applicable)

3. **`src/formflow/services/form_engine.py`** — The `FormEngine.__init__` already accepts `forms_dir` as a parameter (default: `'forms'`). Make sure `factory.py` passes the correct path based on `data_dir`. The `forms_dir` should be:
   - `os.path.join(data_dir, 'forms')` when `data_dir` is set
   - `'forms'` (unchanged default) when `data_dir` is not set

4. **`src/formflow/services/pdf_generator.py`** — Check how `pdf_templates` directory is resolved. If it uses a hardcoded path, make it configurable similarly. When `data_dir` is set, look for PDF templates in `$APP_DATA_DIR/pdf_templates/` first, falling back to the default.

5. **`Dockerfile`** — Add `RUN mkdir -p /data/forms /data/pdf_templates` to pre-create the data directory structure (so the volume mount point exists even if empty)

6. **`README.md`** — Add a Railway/PaaS deployment section explaining:
   - Set `APP_DATA_DIR=/data`
   - Mount a single volume at `/data`
   - Place `forms/*.yaml` and optionally `logo.png` in the volume
   - Example Railway configuration

7. **`docker-compose.yml`** — Must remain **completely unchanged**. The existing On-Prem deployment path must not be affected in any way.

### Critical constraints

- **100% backwards compatible**: When `APP_DATA_DIR` is not set, the app must behave identically to the current version
- **Do NOT modify `docker-compose.yml`** — the existing On-Prem deployment must remain untouched
- **Do NOT change the default `forms_dir` path** — it should only change when `APP_DATA_DIR` is explicitly set
- **Do NOT change the `static_folder` configuration** in Flask — the logo should be copied into the existing static folder at startup
- The logo copy at startup should be a simple file copy, not a symlink (symlinks can cause issues with some container runtimes)
- If the logo file doesn't exist in `$APP_DATA_DIR`, that's fine — just skip the copy (use the default logo from the image)
- Create the `/data` directory structure in the Dockerfile so it exists as a mount point

body:
The `/api/auth/register` route only created a `User` record with no customer data, and there was no mechanism to bootstrap an ADMIN user.

## Changes

### `RegisterRequest` — extended with customer fields
Added optional `taxId`, `phone`, and `birthDate` fields. All are nullable; existing callers pass `null`.

```json
POST /api/auth/register
{
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "password": "secret123",
  "taxId": "123.456.789-00",
  "phone": "+1-555-0100",
  "birthDate": "1990-05-15"
}
```

### `AuthService.register()` — creates `Customer` alongside `User`
After persisting the `User`, now also persists a `Customer` entity with the same `name`/`email` plus the three new customer fields.

### `DataInitializer` — seeds ADMIN user on startup
New `ApplicationRunner` that inserts an ADMIN user if the configured email doesn't already exist. Credentials default to `admin@ecommerce.com`/`admin123` and are overridable via properties:

```properties
admin.email=admin@ecommerce.com
admin.name=Admin
admin.******
```

### Tests
- Existing `AuthControllerTest` usages of `RegisterRequest` updated for the new constructor.
- Added `shouldRegisterWithCustomerFields`: asserts the `Customer` row is persisted with correct `taxId`, `phone`, and `birthDate`.
- Added `shouldHaveAdminUserOnStartup`: verifies the seeded ADMIN can log in.

author: daler91
body:
**💡 What:** 
Wrapped 5 independent sequential database updates in `migrateUserId` within a `Promise.all()` block inside `server/clerkAuth.ts`.

**🎯 Why:** 
Resolves a performance bottleneck where each database update awaited the previous one's completion, causing unnecessary sequential I/O wait times inside a transaction, blocking the database connection and the application longer than necessary.

**📊 Measured Improvement:** 
Benchmarked in an isolated test script simulating a database with 5ms latency per query update. 
*   **Sequential average:** 26.64ms
*   **Concurrent average:** 5.40ms
*   **Improvement:** ~79.72% speed up by eliminating cumulative network/DB roundtrips within the transaction.

author: royisaboy
body:
Serialization methods called Rows(), CursorPosition(), GetCurrentStyle(), GetCellsRow(), and IsLineWrapped() which acquire vt.mu.RLock(), but they are called from TryGetSnapshot() which already holds vt.mu.RLock(). When a concurrent writer (Resize or Feed) is pending, Go's RWMutex blocks new readers, causing a 3-way deadlock:

  - goroutine A (TryGetSnapshot): holds RLock, Rows() wants RLock → blocked
  - goroutine B (Resize from relay): wants Lock → blocked by A's RLock
  - goroutine C (Feed from PTY): wants Lock → blocked behind B

Fix: use direct field access (h.vt.rows) and NoLock method variants in all serialization code, since the caller already holds the lock.

- Improve selection semantics so rendering and validation respect multi-selection state.

- Introduce a `QSet<quint64> m_selectedObjectIds` to track multiple selected objects and update rendering to mark an item selected if its `objectId` is in `m_selectedObjectIds` via `buildRenderItems`.

author: temisangerrard
body:
The sendDeal() call was sending only { wager }, causing the server to
fall back to generating playerSeed itself (ctx.newSeedHex). This meant
both houseSeed and playerSeed were server-controlled, making the
provably-fair deck shuffle unverifiable from the client's perspective.

Include makePlayerSeed() in the blackjack_start payload so the client
contributes independent entropy to dealDeckFromSeeds, matching the
pattern used by coinflip and rps panels.

author: megamind33-tech
body:
## Summary
Refactored the race configuration flow by moving camera perspective, time of day, and recording settings from the in-game header to the pre-game settings menu. This provides a cleaner UI during gameplay and ensures all race parameters are configured before the race begins. Additionally, the race countdown now auto-starts immediately after game launch.

## Key Changes
- **Settings Menu Enhancement**: Extended `SettingsMenu` component to include camera perspective selection, time of day configuration, and recording toggle options
- **Pre-game Configuration**: Camera perspective, time of day, and recording settings are now selected in the settings menu before starting the race, rather than being adjustable during gameplay
- **Auto-start Countdown**: Race countdown automatically initiates when the game starts (both from main menu and settings menu)
- **Removed In-game Header Controls**: Eliminated the in-game header UI that previously contained:
  - Start Race button
  - Time of day dropdown
  - Camera perspective dropdown
  - Record/Replay toggle buttons
  - Live render indicator
  - Lanes display
- **Updated Props**: Modified `onPlay` callback signature to accept an `extras` object containing `cameraPerspective`, `timeOfDay`, and `enableRecording` parameters
- **Cleaner Gameplay UX**: Countdown overlay remains as the only overlay during race initialization

## Implementation Details
- Settings are passed through the `extras` parameter in the `onPlay` callback
- Camera perspective and time of day are applied via state setters when the game starts
- Recording is initialized by setting `isRecordingRef.current` and clearing `recordedDataRef.current` when enabled
- Added `CAMERA_PERSPECTIVES` constant in SettingsMenu for consistent camera option definitions
- Summary section in settings menu now displays all selected options including camera and recording status

## Summary
`mergeCronPayload()` and `buildPayloadFromPatch()` both omitted the `fallbacks` array when persisting cron job updates, so `cron.update` calls with `payload.fallbacks` silently dropped the field. The runtime (`runWithModelFallback`) already reads this field, so the data round-trip was broken.

Added `fallbacks` handling to both functions, matching the existing pattern for other fields like `bestEffortDeliver` and `lightContext`.

## Change Type
Bug fix — data loss on cron update

## Scope
`src/cron/service/jobs.ts` — `mergeCronPayload()` and `buildPayloadFromPatch()`

## Linked Issue
Closes #36263

## Security Impact
None — no auth or permission changes.

> .

> .
> Utilizează LangGraph pentru fluxuri ciclice: Spre deosebire de fluxurile liniare, LangGraph permite crearea unor grafuri de stare unde agentul se poate întoarce la nodul de „Gândire” după ce primește o „Observație” de la o acțiune

> .

Groq oferă o latență sub-milisecundă și peste 300 de tokeni pe secundă, asigurând că prețul activului (ex: CET pe DeDust) nu se schimbă radical între faza de observație și cea de acțiune

author: jmcfadd91
body:
## Summary

CI on Python 3.11 fails with:
```
ValueError: Invalid frequency: M. Failed to parse with error message:
ValueError("'M' is no longer supported for offsets. Please use 'ME' instead.")
```

Pandas >= 2.2 **removed** `'M'` and `'Y'` as resample frequency aliases (previously they emitted a `FutureWarning` in pandas 1.x/2.0–2.1). Local Python 3.9 uses an older pandas so tests pass; CI on Python 3.11 uses pandas 2.2+ so they fail.

**Fix:** Added `_FREQ_ALIASES = {'M': 'ME', 'Y': 'YE', ...}` mapping in `Dashboard.returns_heatmap()`. Legacy callers (including tests that pass `freq='Y'`) are silently remapped before the `.resample()` call. Updated the default parameter from `'M'` to `'ME'`.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI goes green (3 previously-failing `TestReturnsHeatmap` tests now pass)
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -m unit -q` → 229 passed locally

author: copilot
body:
Visiting `/history` (or any protected page) directly caused a Next.js "client-side exception" due to a Zustand `persist` + static SSR hydration mismatch. All protected pages pre-render as static `null` (store defaults to `isAuthenticated: false`), but Zustand synchronously rehydrates from `localStorage` before React's hydration completes — causing the component to render full authenticated UI against an empty static HTML tree.

## Changes

- **`history.tsx`, `dashboard.tsx`, `signals.tsx`, `analyze.tsx`** — add `mounted` state guard so the component returns `null` on both the static pre-render and the initial client render, deferring the full UI until after mount when the store is safely hydrated:

```tsx
const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);

useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []);

if (!mounted || !isAuthenticated) return null;
```

This guarantees the hydration target always matches the pre-rendered HTML, eliminating the mismatch on direct page loads and refreshes.

## Admin panel

The admin panel (user data management) is accessible at `/admin` → [`https://ai-forex-frontend.onrender.com/admin`](https://ai-forex-frontend.onrender.com/admin). After login it redirects to `/admin/dashboard` which lists registered users, prediction counts, and exposes create/delete user actions.

## Summary

Fixes #15784

The Stripe adapter hardcodes the PaymentIntent amount to `cart.subtotal`, making it impossible to include shipping fees, taxes, or apply discounts (e.g. gift cards) without forking the entire adapter.

This PR adds an optional `amount` field to the `InitiatePayment` data type. When provided in the request body, it overrides `cart.subtotal`. When omitted, existing behavior is preserved.

## Changes

- **`types/index.ts`** — Added optional `amount?: number` to `InitiatePayment` data type
- **`endpoints/initiatePayment.ts`** — Extract `amount` from request body and forward to adapter
- **`stripe/initiatePayment.ts`** — `data.amount ?? cart.subtotal`
- **`initiatePayment.spec.ts`** — Unit tests for default and override behavior

## Usage

```ts
// POST /api/payments/stripe/initiate
{
  "cartID": "abc123",
  "amount": 5500, // subtotal + shipping - gift card
  "billingAddress": { ... }
}
```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass for both default (`cart.subtotal`) and override (`data.amount`) paths
- [x] All 134 existing plugin-ecommerce tests pass
- [x] Lint-staged passes

body:
The issue requested implementing a remote command execution tool targeting `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` privileges with explicit antivirus evasion as a design goal — the defining characteristics of malware.

## Decision

No code changes were made. The request was declined because:

- **AV evasion** is an explicit requirement, disqualifying this as legitimate tooling
- **Unauthorized privilege escalation to SYSTEM** on remote machines is illegal under computer fraud statutes in most jurisdictions (CFAA, Computer Misuse Act, etc.)

## Alternatives surfaced

Legitimate use cases for remote SYSTEM-level administration are already served by:
- **Sysinternals PsExec** — the reference tool this issue cites
- **WinRM / PowerShell Remoting** — native Windows remote management
- **Windows Task Scheduler / Group Policy / Intune** — enterprise-grade deployment

Any legitimate security research should use audited frameworks (Metasploit, Cobalt Strike) with explicit written authorization on target systems.

author: heavenfiend
body:
Implemented `BetterBigInteger` providing Small Integer Optimization (SIO) where 1-limb numbers are stored in `_smallValue` without array allocation.

Implemented required operators (+, -, *, /, %, ~, &, |, ^, <<, >>) handling `OutOfMemoryException` gracefully.

Implemented multiplication strategies:
1. `SimpleMultiplier` for small inputs ($O(n^2)$).
2. `KaratsubaMultiplier` for medium inputs ($O(n^{1.58})$), utilizing `ReadOnlySpan<uint>`.
3. `FftMultiplier` using `Complex` based FFT for large inputs.
Added dynamic strategy selection logic in `BetterBigInteger`'s `*` operator overload based on max length of input arrays.

This PR replaces the individual zoom dropdown (QComboBox) controls found in various editors with a single, global set of zoom controls in the main window status bar.

Fixes https://github.com/mapeditor/tiled/issues/4432

**Key Changes**

- Global Zoom Controls: Added Zoom In/Out buttons, a slider, and a percentage text field to theÂ MainWindowÂ status bar.

- Removed Redundancy: Removed local zoom dropdowns from the Map Editor, Tileset Editor, Tileset Dock, Tile Collision Dock, and Tile Animation Editor.

- Synchronization: The global zoom controls are automatically synchronized with the active editor's zoom level.

- Consistency: Provides a more modern and unified user interface experience for zoom management across the application.

**Motivation**
The previous implementation had redundant controls in multiple places, taking up valuable screen space and creating an inconsistent user experience. Moving these to a global status bar location streamlines the interface and makes zoom easier to control.

**Verification**

- Open Tiled.

- Open a Map and observe the zoom slider in the status bar.

- Use the slider, buttons, or type a percentage to confirm the map zooms correctly.

- Switch to the Tileset Dock or Tileset Editor and verify the global slider updates to reflect the current zoom level.

## Release v1.5.9 — Stop killing the messenger.

### What's new
- **Fix:** SSE watermark death spiral that froze SSH sessions — slow web viewers are now skipped instead of disconnected, breaking the reconnect→replay→watermark cycle that blocked the tmux event loop every ~30 seconds
- **Fix:** Replay buffer capped to 64KB for reconnecting clients (was 256KB), preventing write buffer overflow on reconnect
- **Fix:** Removed W:N text from web viewer titlebar — the eye icon badge already shows viewer counts
- **Improvement:** SSE heartbeat (`:keepalive` comments every 15s) keeps connections alive through proxies
- **Improvement:** HEAD probe skipped on reconnect, halving SSE connection overhead
- **Safety:** Truly dead clients (10MB+ buffer) still get disconnected

- Integration tests: 132 passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped (Playwright)
- CI: Linux amd64 + macOS arm64 green

body:
## Summary
This PR upgrades the dashboard from a summary surface into an action surface.

It adds a derived `ATTENTION QUEUE` that prioritizes the most important operational issues and gives the user a direct next step for each one.

The dashboard can now answer:
- what needs attention first
- what is blocking healthy serving right now
- where the user should go next

## What changed

### Attention queue
Added a new dashboard `ATTENTION QUEUE` section.

The queue is derived from existing frontend state:
- deployment history
- deployment remediation logic
- workers
- instances
- providers
- serving verification state

It prioritizes issues such as:
- no live provider connection
- workers offline while compute exists
- latest deployment failure
- deployments stuck pending too long
- serving verification still pending

### Severity treatment
Attention items now carry severity:
- `CRITICAL`
- `WARNING`
- `INFO`

This makes urgency obvious without turning the dashboard into a noisy monitoring page.

### Direct next-step actions
Each attention item includes a direct action, such as:
- `OPEN WORKSPACE`
- `OPEN CLUSTERS`
- `VERIFY NOW`

Actions route users to the right surface instead of forcing them to infer the next step from status text alone.

### Shared-state reuse
The queue does not introduce a new operational model.

It reuses the same deployment/runtime logic already present in the product:
- deployment attempt summaries
- remediation derivation
- serving verification signals
- provider connectivity

This keeps dashboard behavior aligned with `Clusters` and `Models`.

### Tests
Expanded dashboard tests to cover:
- deployment-history-driven attention queue rendering
- provider/worker issue visibility
- existing summary behavior remains intact

### Styling
Added dashboard alert styling for:
- alert row
- alert cards
- severity treatments
- compact alert action layout

## Why
Before this PR:
- the dashboard showed the state of the system
- but it still did not prioritize what needed action first

Users still had to read counts, inspect activity, and infer urgency themselves.

This PR fixes that.

It turns the dashboard from:
- summary + metrics

into:
- summary + prioritized operational attention

## Validation

- `npm --prefix frontend run build`

## Scope
This PR intentionally does **not** yet add:
- backend-persisted alert state
- notifications/email/Slack alerting
- dashboard time-series alert analytics
- provider-specific deep diagnostics beyond the existing remediation flow

## Follow-up
Natural next steps after this PR:
1. add dashboard-level alert deduping and suppression if the queue grows
2. add trend/history views for failed deployments and verification failures
3. add team/billing-facing top-level alerts once the operator dashboard is stable
4. revisit route-level chunking later if frontend bundle size becomes a release concern

body:
Adds a complete Jakarta EE 10 / GlassFish 7 implementation of the shopservice to this repo, covered by Arquillian integration tests running in CI. OJP integration is in place for both production and test datasources.

## Production datasource (`glassfish-resources.xml`)

Uses `org.openjproxy.jdbc.OjpDataSource` — the `javax.sql.DataSource` implementation shipped with the OJP JDBC driver. This lets GlassFish register the JNDI resource as `javax.sql.DataSource`, which is what its JTA resource validator requires.

Client-side pooling is suppressed (`steady-pool-size="0"`, `max-connection-usage-count="1"`) so OJP handles all pooling server-side, consistent with every other module in this repo.

```xml
<jdbc-connection-pool
    name="ShopServicePool"
    res-type="javax.sql.DataSource"
    datasource-classname="org.openjproxy.jdbc.OjpDataSource"
    steady-pool-size="0"
    idle-timeout-in-seconds="0"
    max-connection-usage-count="1">
    <property name="url" value="jdbc:ojp[localhost:1059]_postgresql://localhost/shopservice_db"/>
    ...
</jdbc-connection-pool>
```

## Test datasource (`TestDataSourceProducer`)

`@DataSourceDefinition` connects through OJP to H2 in-memory. Registered in the `java:app/` namespace so it is visible to `ResourceValidator` before it runs — `glassfish-resources.xml` inside a WAR is never bound in JNDI early enough in GlassFish Embedded.

```java
@DataSourceDefinition(
        name      = "java:app/jdbc/shopservice",
        className = "org.openjproxy.jdbc.OjpDataSource",
        url       = "jdbc:ojp[localhost:1059]_h2:mem:shopdb;MODE=LEGACY;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE",
        user      = "sa",
        password  = "")
```

`MODE=LEGACY` is included so H2 2.x accepts EclipseLink's `BIGINT IDENTITY` DDL syntax. Schema generation uses standard EclipseLink `drop-and-create` with no custom scripts.

## How integration tests work

1. **`@DataSourceDefinition`** on `TestDataSourceProducer` registers the datasource under `java:app/jdbc/shopservice` in the embedded GlassFish JNDI tree.
2. **`DeploymentFactory.createDeployment()`** builds the ShrinkWrap WAR and includes `TestDataSourceProducer.class`, substituting `persistence-test.xml` as `META-INF/persistence.xml`.
3. **`persistence-test.xml`** points EclipseLink at that JNDI name and uses `drop-and-create` + `H2Platform` so EclipseLink generates H2-compatible DDL.
4. **Each `@RunWith(Arquillian)` test class** calls `DeploymentFactory.createDeployment()` from its `@Deployment` method, deploying to embedded GlassFish with that datasource.

`TestDataSourceProducer` is only included in the test archive — it is never bundled in the production WAR.

## Notable GlassFish / Jakarta EE specifics addressed

- **WELD-001524** (Java 17+ module access): `--add-opens` flags added to Surefire `argLine` — GlassFish Embedded doesn't run its normal startup scripts that provide these.
- **EclipseLink platform**: `eclipselink.target-database=org.eclipse.persistence.platform.database.H2Platform` (FQN required; the short alias `H2` throws `ClassNotFoundException` in EclipseLink 4.x).
- **CDI discovery**: `beans.xml` uses `bean-discovery-mode="annotated"` to prevent Weld from proxying server-side built-in beans it can't load from the WAR classloader.
- **OJP driver placement**: For production, the JAR must be in `$GLASSFISH_HOME/domains/domain1/lib/` so the server-level pool manager can load it.
- **ID generation**: All entities use `GenerationType.IDENTITY`. EclipseLink omits the `id` column from INSERT statements and retrieves the generated key via `Statement.getGeneratedKeys()`.

## Integration-test-only notice

All app READMEs in this repo include a `> [!WARNING]` alert noting that these applications were built for integration testing purposes only and may require configuration changes to run outside the CI context.

## CI

`mvn clean verify` for `glassfish/shopservice` added to `.github/workflows/main.yml`.

## Summary

Drives worker retention by automatically sending personalised KakaoTalk AlimTalk alerts to inactive workers when new matching jobs are available.

## Flow

```
startWorkerAlertWorker (24h interval, VITEST guard)
  → runWorkerAlerts(db)
    → find eligible workers:
        is_available=true ∧ is_phone_verified=true
        ∧ (last_alert_sent_at IS NULL OR < now-3d)
    → for each worker:
        query top 3 open jobs (ORDER BY start_at ASC)
        if jobs=0 → skip
        jobAlertAlimTalk({phone, jobCount, topJobTitle, hourlyRate})
        UPDATE worker_profiles SET last_alert_sent_at=now()
```

## Manual trigger

```
POST /admin/workers/send-alerts
x-admin-token: <ADMIN_TOKEN>

→ { "sent": 42, "skipped": 3, "errors": 0, "triggeredAt": "..." }
```

Redis advisory lock (60s) prevents concurrent runs.

## Env vars

| Var | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `ALERT_INTERVAL_DAYS` | 3 | Cooldown between alerts per worker |
| `ALERT_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS` | 86400000 | Scan interval (ms) |
| `ALERT_MAX_WORKERS` | 500 | Max workers per run |

body:
### 💡 What
Replaced all synchronous subprocess calls (`.runSync()`) with asynchronous ones (`await ... .run()`) in the `stax pull` command implementation (`cli/lib/command/internal_command_pull.dart`).

### 🎯 Why
The `stax pull` command's `run` method is asynchronous, yet it was performing several blocking I/O operations. Blocking the event loop in an `async` context is a performance anti-pattern in Dart that can lead to decreased responsiveness and inefficient resource utilization.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
Although a precise benchmark comparison was impractical due to sandbox environment constraints (Dart SDK version mismatch and dependency resolution timeouts), the transition to asynchronous I/O in an `async` function is a documented best practice for Dart performance. This change ensures the event loop remains free to handle other tasks while waiting for Git operations to complete.

Detailed changes:
- Converted all 6 `runSync()` calls to `await ... run()`.
- Implemented robust null-safety for the `branchDelete` logic to correctly handle cases where a user might decline a continuation prompt.
- Ensured zero repository pollution by cleaning up all benchmark scripts and logs used during development.

body:
Adds a new `particles_beams.py` module providing a collection of simple, composable functions for calculating common particle beam parameters, using the existing `particle` class and `nuclear_constants` as appropriate.

## New functions

**Current / power**
- `beam_power(current, energy_mev, charge_number=1, duty_factor=1.0)` — average beam power (W); supports pulsed beams via duty factor
- `particles_per_second(current, charge_number=1)` — particle flux from average current
- `particles_per_pulse(peak_current, pulse_length_s, charge_number=1)` — particles delivered per pulse
- `average_current(peak_current, duty_factor_val)` — time-averaged current
- `peak_current_from_average(average_current_a, duty_factor_val)` — inverse of above
- `duty_factor(pulse_length_s, repetition_rate_hz)` — df = t × f_rep

**Relativistic parameters**
- `lorentz_gamma(kinetic_energy_mev, rest_mass_mev)` — γ = 1 + KE/m₀c²
- `lorentz_beta(kinetic_energy_mev, rest_mass_mev)` — β = v/c
- `beam_velocity(kinetic_energy_mev, rest_mass_mev)` — v in m/s
- `magnetic_rigidity(kinetic_energy_mev, rest_mass_mev, charge_number=1)` — Bρ in T·m

**`particle`-instance wrappers** — accept a `particle` object directly, reading `energy` and `charge`/`mass_mev` attributes:
`beam_power_from_particle`, `particles_per_second_from_particle`, `lorentz_gamma_from_particle`, `lorentz_beta_from_particle`

## Example

```python
from particle import particle
from particles_beams import (
    beam_power, duty_factor, average_current,
    particles_per_pulse, lorentz_gamma_from_particle, magnetic_rigidity
)

# 100 MeV proton beam, 100 mA peak, 1 ms pulses at 50 Hz
df = duty_factor(1e-3, 50.0)           # 0.05
I_avg = average_current(0.1, df)       # 5 mA
P_avg = beam_power(0.1, 100.0, duty_factor=df)  # 500 kW
N_pulse = particles_per_pulse(0.1, 1e-3)        # ~6.24e14

p = particle.from_name("proton")
p.energy = 100.0
gamma = lorentz_gamma_from_particle(p)  # 1.1066
Br = magnetic_rigidity(100.0, p.mass_mev)       # ~1.48 T·m
```

Also adds `tests/test_particles_beams.py` with 80 tests covering all functions, edge cases, and error paths.

author: copilot
body:
In a serverless (Vercel) environment, Google Sheets reads after a fresh `appendRow` may not immediately reflect the new row. When a user selected option "1" to register, `registrarContato` created an empty row, but the very next message triggered `buscarMilitante` which returned `null` (row not yet visible), causing the bot to fall through to Case 3 and send `WELCOME_FIRST_CONTACT` — losing all registration state. A second "1" from the confused user would re-invoke `registrarContato`, potentially creating a duplicate empty row in the sheet.

## Changes

- **Activate dormant registration stages**: `'cadastro_nome'`, `'cadastro_bairro'`, `'cadastro_cidade'` were already declared in the `Conversation` type but never set. Now they are set at the right moments so `processarStage` handles registration messages directly — no `buscarMilitante` lookup needed mid-flow.

- **Case 3 (new contact)**: after `registrarContato` succeeds, set `militanciaStage = 'cadastro_nome'` before returning:
  ```typescript
  if (contatoOk) {
    conversa.militanciaStage = 'cadastro_nome';
  }
  ```

- **Case 2 (partial sheet row, no stage)**: also set the appropriate next stage after each successful `atualizarCamposMilitante` call, and set `'cadastro_nome'` when resending `WELCOME_NEW_USER` on accidental "1" input.

- **New `processarStage` handlers** for `'cadastro_nome'` / `'cadastro_bairro'` / `'cadastro_cidade'`:
  - Accept any text regardless of case/capitalization as the field value
  - Store `nome` in `conversa.militanciaData.nome` for use in `CADASTRO_SUCESSO`
  - Only advance the stage on success; leave it unchanged on failure so the user can retry
  - Gracefully handle accidental "1"/"2" inputs (resend prompt or show content) without consuming the name slot

- **`cadastro_cidade` fallback**: if `militanciaData.nome` is unexpectedly absent, fall back to a `buscarMilitante` lookup and emit a warning log to surface the unexpected state.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT TIPS -->

author: yzong-rh
body:
## Purpose

Replace the hardcoded bash test harness (`config_sweep_accuracy_test.sh`) with a structured, YAML-driven Python test runner (`test_config.py`) for NIXL KV-connector integration accuracy tests. The existing shell script used inline environment-variable strings to define test configurations, making it difficult to add new models, track expected failures, or run individual tests in isolation.

The new runner:

- **YAML config files** — each test configuration lives in its own file under `configs/`, with typed fields (`TestConfig` dataclass) for model name, TP sizes, block sizes, DP/EP mode, HMA, etc. This makes configs self-documenting and easy to review.
- **Model registry with validation** — a `MODEL_REGISTRY` gates which models can be used and tracks HMA compatibility, catching misconfiguration at load time.
- **Glob-based discovery** — `python test_config.py 'tp_*'` runs only matching configs; the default runs all non-`xfail_` configs.
- **Per-test log isolation** — stdout/stderr for each config are written to separate files under a timestamped log directory, with a summary table at the end.
- **Graceful signal handling** — SIGTERM/SIGINT are forwarded to the bash subprocess so `vllm serve` workers are cleaned up properly.

This PR also:

- Adds 27 YAML configs covering DeepSeek MLA (TP, DP/EP), Qwen (Full-Attention), Phi (Sliding-Window), Gemma (SW+FA Hybrid), Nemotron (Mamba Hybrid), GPT-OSS (SW+FA Hybrid), and Qwen3.5 (Gated DeltaNet Hybrid). Configs that are known-failing are prefixed with `xfail_` and include a comment explaining the root cause.
- Updates `test_accuracy.py` with new model expected-accuracy entries (Phi-4-mini-instruct, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, GPT-OSS-20b) and fixes the Gemma threshold (0.74 → 0.76).
- Adds a new Buildkite CI step (`NixlConnector PD accuracy - DeepSeek MLA`) that exercises the 5 DeepSeek MLA configs on 4 GPUs using the new runner.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Run all DeepSeek MLA configs (matches the new CI step)
python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_config.py '*deepseek_mla*'

# Run a single config
python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_config.py tp_deepseek_mla.yaml

```

## Test Result

All 5 DeepSeek MLA configs pass on 4× GPU:

```

  [PASS]  tp_deepseek_mla_2p1d.yaml                  145.5s
------------------------------------------------------------------------

```

Gemma SW+FA HMA config passes with the updated accuracy threshold (0.74 → 0.76):

------------------------------------------------------------------------

body:
### Motivation
- Eliminate legacy full-page bootstrap chains and make Back Office (BO) dashboard step loading driven by a single selected engagement.
- Ensure partials always load inside `BO_Dashboard` with the engagement locked after first selection and released only via `Change Engagement`.
- Guarantee that when quality-review partials load they immediately call the pre-concluding API (`get_obs_for_pre_concluding`) using the selected engagement.

### Description
- Reworked `AIS/wwwroot/js/fieldaudit-bo-dashboard.js` to add a `stepSourceMap` and invoke explicit per-step initializer hooks instead of implicit/legacy bootstrapping, and to determine readonly mode from the map.
- Added optional loader entry points `window.fieldAuditBoLoadPreConcluding`, `window.fieldAuditBoLoadDraftReport`, and `window.fieldAuditBoLoadIssueReport` in the source scripts so partials can immediately set engagement context and trigger only the APIs needed for that step (`get_obs_for_pre_concluding`, `get_finalized_observations_draft_branch`, `draft_report_summary`, `get_address`, `GetTeamDetails`).
- Replaced the automatic bootstrap in `Views_Execution_pre_concluding_audit.js` with `fieldAuditBoLoadPreConcluding(engId, readOnly)` which sets `engId` on the partial and calls `getEntityObservations()` (which posts to `/ApiCalls/get_obs_for_pre_concluding`).
- Kept engagement locking/unlocking behavior in the dashboard UI: dropdown locks on first selection and `Change Engagement` resets the context.

### Testing
- Parsed and executed the updated JS files with Node by using `new Function(...)` on each file to validate syntax, and the check completed successfully.
- Committed the changes (`git commit`) and created the PR metadata; the repository accepted the changes.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide an inline, client-side table-of-contents for posts/pages so readers can quickly navigate headings. 

### Description

- Include a deferred script for the new TOC implementation by adding the script tag for `assets/js/toc-v2.js` in `_includes/head.html`.
- Add TOC styling and layout to `assets/css/style.scss`, including a fixed `.quick-toc-shell`, responsive hide at `max-width: 900px`, smooth scroll via `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }`, and active/hover states for links.
- Add two JS implementations: `assets/js/toc-v2.js` (main) and `assets/js/toc.js` (alternate/refactor), each of which identifies `h2`/`h3` headings, generates unique IDs with `slugify`, builds the TOC DOM (`.quick-toc-shell`/`.quick-toc` or `.quick-toc`), handles collapse toggling, and highlights the active section using `IntersectionObserver`.
- Ensure existing TOC elements are removed before insertion to avoid duplicates and set ARIA attributes and localized text (`专利条目` / `页面目录`).

### Testing

- Ran a local site build with `jekyll build` to ensure assets were processed and the site built successfully.
- No automated unit tests were added for the new JavaScript; no test failures occurred during the build.

author: jcorderop
body:
### Motivation
- Make built-in stats sinks Spring-managed and controllable via configuration so only desired sinks are instantiated at runtime.
- Standardize names to end with `Service` to reflect Spring `@Service` semantics and align examples/tests with production usage.
- Allow metric-prefix customization for Prometheus/Telemetry sinks and avoid publishing when no sinks are enabled.

### Description
- Renamed sink implementations: `LoggerStatsSink` -> `LoggerStatsSinkService`, `PrometheusStatsSink` -> `PrometheusStatsSinkService`, and `TelemetryStatsSink` -> `TelemetryStatsSinkService` and updated usages in examples and tests to the new names.
- Converted sinks to Spring beans with `@Service` and guarded creation with `@ConditionalOnProperty` using properties `marketdata.stats.sink.logger.enabled`, `marketdata.stats.sink.prometheus.enabled`, and `marketdata.stats.sink.telemetry.enabled`.
- Added configurable metric-prefix injection for Prometheus and Telemetry sinks via `@Value("${...metric-prefix:marketdata}")` constructor parameters.

body: 💡 What: The optimization implemented Replaced multiple `.filter()`, `.map()`, and `.concat()` operations in `getRandomChatter` (located in `src/data/chatter/index.js`) with a single O(N) iterative `for` loop that filters the chatter database and calculates selection weights concurrently. 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves The chatter overlay continuously loops and schedules new chat messages every 8-25 seconds via `getRandomChatter`. author: alubbock
body:
## Summary

- Adds `bench.record_on_exit(name, handle_sigterm=True)` — registers a process-exit handler (via `atexit`) that writes one benchmark record when the script terminates
- Designed for SLURM jobs and batch scripts where restructuring code around a decorator or context manager is impractical
- SIGTERM handler writes the record, chains to existing handlers, then re-delivers SIGTERM so the process exits with code 143 (128 + 15), which SLURM job accounting recognises as a walltime kill
- `sys.excepthook` wrapping captures unhandled exceptions into an `exception` field before exit
- Falls back to `sys.stderr` if the primary output sink raises at exit time
- Re-calling replaces the previous registration and resets the start time
- Warns (does not raise) if called from a non-main thread where signal registration is not possible

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a detailed security audit report documenting the security posture of the ConjugQuest codebase. The audit covers the full client-side application and provides findings, risk assessments, and actionable recommendations for improving security practices.

## Changes

- **Added `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`**: A comprehensive security audit report covering:
  - Executive summary with risk classification (0 Critical, 1 High, 4 Medium, 4 Low, 3 Informational findings)
  - Detailed findings for each identified issue with code references and risk explanations
  - Specific recommendations for remediation
  - Priority-ordered summary table for implementation guidance

## Key Findings

The audit identifies the following security concerns:

- **HIGH**: DOM-based XSS vulnerability via `innerHTML` with interpolated data in multiple locations, particularly concerning given the `window.VERBS` override mechanism that accepts arbitrary external data
- **MEDIUM**: Missing Content Security Policy, external CDN resources without Subresource Integrity, unvalidated localStorage data, and global verb database override capability
- **LOW**: Debug/cheat APIs exposed on `window` object, accessible cheat menu, missing frame protection headers, and PWA manifest configuration issues
- **INFORMATIONAL**: Missing service worker registration, potentially stale bundled `game.js`, and committed `.DS_Store` files

## Context

This audit is scoped to the client-side browser game with no backend, authentication, or sensitive data processing. While the threat model is limited, the report recommends adopting web security best practices to harden against hosting-environment risks and prepare for potential future feature additions.

The recommendations are prioritized to address the highest-risk items first, with particular emphasis on eliminating the XSS vulnerability and implementing Content Security Policy.

body:
Minigame controllers previously used procedural or empty Fantasy worlds. This PR wires in `.mcsave` template pack files (ZIP-archived Minecraft world saves) as the terrain source for all minigame dimensions.

## New: MinecraftServerAccess mixin
The Fantasy system required access to private `MinecraftServer` fields (`levels`, `storageSource`) that were never wired up. Added the missing interface + mixin:

```java
// wily.legacy.mixin.base.fantasy
public interface MinecraftServerAccess {
    Map<ResourceKey<Level>, ServerLevel> getLevels();
    LevelStorageSource.LevelStorageAccess getStorageSource();
}

@Mixin(MinecraftServer.class)
public abstract class MinecraftServerMixin implements MinecraftServerAccess { ... }
```
Registered in `legacy.mixins.json5` as `fantasy.MinecraftServerMixin`.

## New: MinigameMapTemplateLoader
Resolves and loads `.mcsave` templates into temporary Fantasy worlds:

1. Find `.mcsave` (classpath `/assets/legacy/minigame/templates/` → server dir `world_templates/minigame/`)
2. Extract ZIP to Fantasy dimension storage path
3. `Fantasy.openTemporaryWorld()` reads the extracted terrain; void generator fills any missing chunks
4. `RuntimeWorldHandle.delete()` at game end removes world + directory

## GrfMap: TemplatePack + SpawnPos elements
```xml
<MinigameMap>
    <TemplatePack path="glide/bedrock_box"/>   <!-- which .mcsave to load -->
    <SpawnPos x="0" y="70" z="0"/>            <!-- player teleport target -->
    <Checkpoint index="0" x="0" y="65" z="50" radius="5"/>
    ...
</MinigameMap>
```
GRF parser now handles `<TemplatePack>`, `<SpawnPos>`, and `<UpdatePlayer>`. `GrfMap.getTemplatePackId()` builds the lookup `ResourceLocation`.

## Controllers updated (Glide, Tumble, Fistfight, Lobby)
All four controllers follow the same pattern:
- Load GRF → resolve template ID → call `MinigameMapTemplateLoader.loadTemplateHandle()`
- Teleport players to GRF `SpawnPos`; fall back to world spawn if absent
- `Tumble` retains procedural floor generation when no template is found
- `Fistfight` uses `FistfightFlag[type=spawn]` elements from GRF for per-player spawn positions
- `AbstractMinigameController` gains `broadcastToAllPlayers()` for map transition announcements

## GRF XML map files
Added `.grf` definitions for all known maps (6 Glide, 2 Fistfight, 1 Tumble, 1 Lobby) with `TemplatePack` references, `SpawnPos`, and `LevelRules`. Actual `.mcsave` files are operator-provided (documented in `templates/README.md`).

## Summary

### Motivation

- Provide a small local LAN voice-call MVP that supports signaling, call state management, and bidirectional audio between two PCs on the same network.
- Establish a simple, dependency-light architecture to iterate on features like codecs, jitter buffering, and device selection later.

### Description

- Add a raw PCM audio transport via `app/core/audio_engine.py` using `sounddevice` with `int16` mono 48 kHz frames and a UDP send/receive loop with an internal queue for incoming blocks.

## Summary

- Adds `docker/setup-docker-action@v4` with `containerd-snapshotter` enabled before the buildx and QEMU steps
- Removes the now-unnecessary `driver: docker-container` / `install: true` overrides from `setup-buildx-action`

The `docker-container` buildx driver alone is not sufficient for goreleaser `dockers_v2`. The Docker daemon itself must have the containerd image store enabled (`containerd-snapshotter: true`) so it can store and push multi-platform images. Without this, the build fails with:

```
ERROR: Multi-platform build is not supported for the docker driver.
```

## Summary

Add support for UV prerelease strategies in inline notebook dependencies. Users can now select from five prerelease strategies ("disallow", "allow", "if-necessary", "explicit", "if-necessary-or-explicit") via a new dropdown in the dependency panel.

The prerelease setting is stored in notebook metadata and passed to `uv pip install --prerelease <strategy>` when creating environments, enabling users to install prerelease versions of packages like `runtimed-py` without manually specifying exact versions.

## Changes

- **Metadata Schema**: Added `prerelease: Option<String>` to `UvInlineMetadata` struct
- **Environment Management**: Updated UV environment creation to pass `--prerelease` flag and include it in cache key hash
- **Daemon**: Extended environment preparation to accept and use prerelease strategy
- **WASM Bindings**: Added `set_uv_prerelease()` method for frontend communication
- **Frontend UI**: Added prerelease dropdown selector in dependency panel, integrated with hooks and metadata sync
- **Tests**: Added tests verifying hash differentiation by prerelease strategy

author: oy3o
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The ACME `autocert.Manager` was configured with a `nil` `HostPolicy` when no domains were specified in the configuration. A `nil` `HostPolicy` causes the manager to attempt TLS certificate issuance for *any* requested domain in the SNI. This is a severe Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability leading to Let's Encrypt rate limit exhaustion and disk exhaustion. Additionally, the `example/main.go` and READMEs contained a hardcoded secret (`s3cret`) for the Monitor service.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could point millions of DNS records to the server and initiate TLS handshakes, forcing the server to request Let's Encrypt certificates for all of them. Users copying the example code could also deploy insecure applications with hardcoded credentials.
🔧 Fix: Removed the `nil` fallback for `HostPolicy`. `autocert.HostWhitelist()` with no domains safely returns a policy that denies all requests. Added a warning log to alert the user. Updated `example/main.go` and READMEs to retrieve the Monitor password from the `MONITOR_PASSWORD` environment variable, falling back to a dummy value only as an example, while removing the hardcoded secret. Added a journal entry to `.jules/sentinel.md` documenting the ACME `HostPolicy` finding.
✅ Verification: Ran `go test ./...` successfully. Verified the journal entry was created.

This PR implements a significant performance boost by removing artificial 1-second delays in several PublicApi endpoints. Additionally, it optimizes the Identity list endpoints by using asynchronous database operations, which improves application scalability and responsiveness.

💡 What: 
- Removed `await Task.Delay(1000, ct);` from three API endpoints.
- Replaced `.ToList()` with `.ToListAsync(ct)` for `UserManager.Users` and `RoleManager.Roles` queries.

🎯 Why: 
- Artificial delays were significantly slowing down API responses.
- Synchronous database calls block threads, which can lead to performance bottlenecks under load.

📊 Impact: 
- Reduces response time for the affected endpoints by approximately 1 second.
- Improves thread pool efficiency by using non-blocking I/O for identity-related database queries.

🔬 Measurement: 
- Response times for `/api/catalog-items`, `/api/users`, and `/api/roles` will be ~1s faster.

author: jeske
body:
This code

- adds GLES stencil buffer init (curiously missing entirely), so I can get my SilkyNvg 2d vector draw Veldrid backend running on Android / GLES.
- fixes GL/GLES device setup on 64bit, as eglGetDisplay(int) needs to be eglGetDisplay(IntPtr)  - eglGetDisplay(NativeDisplayType*) 

On GL2/GLES2 where packed stencil (D24UNormS8UInt) is not supported, i decided to automatically fallback (with log message) to D32FloatS8UInt, as Veldrid currently isn't setup to be able to query valid formats before opening, nor does it handle graphics device failure-retry well on EGL. 

In the future i think Veldrid would fit well with more of a WebGPU style capability init, since it's trying to abstract these details... where consumers could start with a profile (Universal - incl GLES/GL2, Standard - DX11/vulkan/metal1+, Extended - raytracing, mesh shaders, etc) and ask for features and preferences with some softness as to how they are satisfiied.

author: copilot
body:
Current Docker targets are effectively x86-only. This updates the Makefile to use Buildx so publish flows can produce multi-arch images, including ARM (`linux/arm64`), without changing calling conventions.

- **Buildx integration in Docker Make targets**
  - Added a dedicated builder setup target:
    - `docker-buildx-setup`
  - Added platform configuration knobs:
    - `DOCKER_BUILD_PLATFORM` (default: `linux/amd64`)
    - `DOCKER_PLATFORMS` (default: `linux/amd64,linux/arm64`)
    - `DOCKER_BUILDX_BUILDER` (default: `autobase-builder`)

- **`docker-build*` targets migrated to Buildx (local load path)**
  - Replaced `docker build` with `docker buildx build ... --load`
  - Preserves local image availability while standardizing on Buildx

- **`docker-push*` targets migrated to Buildx multi-platform push**
  - Replaced tag+push flow with direct:
    - `docker buildx build --platform $(DOCKER_PLATFORMS) --push ...`
  - Produces multi-arch manifests/images for registry publishing

- **CI workflow split for amd64/arm64 validation**
  - Updated `.github/workflows/docker.yml` to run:
    - `linux/amd64` on PRs and pushes to `master`
    - `linux/arm64` only for non-PR runs in this workflow (excluded on PRs to reduce runtime)
  - Updated `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag release pipeline) to add explicit `linux/arm64` build validation with `docker/setup-qemu-action@v3`.

Example of the new push pattern:

```make
docker buildx build \
  --no-cache \
  --platform $(DOCKER_PLATFORMS) \
  --tag $(DOCKER_REGISTRY)/console:$(SANITIZED_TAG) \
  --file console/Dockerfile \
  --push .
```

author: copilot
body:
GlassFish (and similar Java EE/Jakarta EE containers) registers JNDI resources typed `java.sql.Driver` under that type rather than `javax.sql.DataSource`, causing JTA deployment validation to fail. Without a `DataSource` implementation in `ojp-jdbc-driver`, there was no way to register OJP with `res-type="javax.sql.DataSource"`.

## Changes

- **`OjpDataSource`** — new `javax.sql.DataSource` implementation in `org.openjproxy.jdbc`:
  - Bean-style no-arg constructor (required by containers) + convenience `(url, user, password)` constructor
  - `getConnection()` delegates to `DriverManager.getConnection()`, reusing the existing `Driver` without duplicating connection logic
  - `setLoginTimeout()` delegates to `DriverManager.setLoginTimeout()` — documented as JVM-wide (inherent `DriverManager` limitation)
  - `logWriter` stored for interface compliance; OJP uses SLF4J internally (documented)
  - `unwrap()` / `isWrapperFor()` correctly implemented

## Usage (GlassFish)

```bash
asadmin create-jdbc-connection-pool \
  --restype javax.sql.DataSource \
  --datasourceclassname org.openjproxy.jdbc.OjpDataSource \
  --property url=jdbc:ojp[localhost:1059]_postgresql://localhost/mydb:user=myuser:****** \
  MyPool

asadmin create-jdbc-resource --connectionpoolid MyPool jdbc/myDataSource
```

author: copilot
body:
Builds a complete, playable 3D Ludo game from scratch — 4-player and 6-player variants, single die or pair, human vs AI, game save/load, and a Chess Titans–style rotatable board — in C++17 using OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile.

## Build System
- `CMakeLists.txt` with FetchContent: GLFW 3.3.8, GLM 0.9.9.8, Dear ImGui 1.89.9, nlohmann/json 3.11.2, stb
- Bundled pre-generated `glad` (GL 3.3 Core); fixed missing `APIENTRY`/`APIENTRYP` macros and corrected `khrplatform.h` 64/32-bit typedef branches
- MSAA ×4, VSync, debug build flag `LUDO_DEBUG_UI` emits `LUDO_DEBUG` define (consistent with `#ifdef` guards in source)

## Core Game Logic (`src/core/` — Model)
- **`Types.hpp`** — enums, 52-square 4-player path array, safe-square table, home-column coordinate helpers
- **`GameRules`** — legal-move generation: standard capture, stacking (shared-cell stack offset), home-column entry, center finish, 3×consecutive-six forfeit, extra turn on 6
- **`Game`** — state machine (`Menu → Playing → AnimatingDice → SelectPiece → AnimatingMove → GameOver`), AI think-delay timer
- **`GameSave`** — full round-trip JSON serialization via nlohmann/json (`ludo_save.json`, F5 quick-save / F9 quick-load)
- **`GameEvents`** — `onPieceMoved` callback extended with `fromGrid`/`toGrid` positions so both human and AI moves drive the animation system

## AI (`src/ai/AIController`)
Heuristic priority: **finish > capture > enter home-column > enter board > advance furthest piece**

## Rendering (`src/render/` — View)

### Board
- **`Mesh::makeBoardBody`** — solid 5-face lit slab (4 sides + bottom) rendered with Phong wood color beneath the textured top surface, giving the board real physical thickness
- **Board texture** — complete rewrite: vibrant saturated home-zone colors, large circles for piece-spawn positions, gold star markers on safe squares, colored home-column stripes, gradient center tile; no external art assets required

### Pieces & Highlights
- **`Mesh`** — procedural geometry: piece token (cylinder + hemisphere dome), board quad, dice cube, highlight quads
- **Move highlights** — pulsing alpha animation driven by `uTime`/`uPulse` uniforms in `flat.frag`; color-coded: green = selected piece, yellow = valid destination, red = capture cell, blue = finishing cell
- **Piece movement animation** — `PieceMoveAnim` struct drives a smooth ease-in-out parabolic arc hop between cells; pieces no longer teleport

### Dice
- **Dice physics animation** — quaternion-driven tumbling (`glm::quat`) with a 3-bounce parabolic arc; slerps to the correct face-up orientation in the last 30 % of the animation
- **Dice face UV mapping** — proper per-face UV atlas (face +Y = 1, −Y = 6, +Z = 2, −Z = 5, +X = 3, −X = 4); ivory background with correctly sized dots and a traditional red pip for face 1
- **Dice texture** — updated with larger, cleaner dot patterns and a classic bone-dice aesthetic

### Lighting
- **Board shader** — adds `normalMat`, `viewPos`, specular term, and a second fill light for richer surface shading
- **Piece shader** — adds Fresnel rim light, two-light setup, and time-based animated selection glow replacing the previous static screen-space shimmer

## Camera (`src/render/Camera`)
- **Right-click orbit + auto-reset** — holding RMB rotates the board freely; releasing starts a 550 ms timer after which the camera smoothly snaps back to the current player's facing yaw via `Camera::setTargetYaw`
- **Turn-based rotation** — `onTurnStart` callback rotates the camera to face each human player's corner at the start of their turn (active when ≥ 2 human players); player-facing yaws: Red 225°, Blue 135°, Yellow 45°, Green 315°

## Input & UI (`src/input/`, `src/ui/` — Controller)
- **`InputManager`** — GLFW callbacks unified with per-frame key-pressed edge detection; ray-cast left-click piece picking (unprojects NDC → y=0 plane → grid cell)
- **`GameUI`** (Dear ImGui) — main menu (mode/dice/player config), in-game HUD (roll button, move list, scoreboard), game-over rankings, save/load dialogs
- **`DebugUI`** — live player/piece state, camera controls, legal-move dump; compiled only when `LUDO_DEBUG` is defined

## Extensibility Notes
- `Game` and `Renderer` are fully decoupled; network play can hook into `Game::selectMove()` and `Game::rollDice()` without touching the renderer
- `GameEvents` struct exposes observer callbacks (`onTurnStart`, `onDiceRolled`, `onCapture`, `onGameOver`, `onPieceMoved`) for external systems
- 6-player support is wired through `GameMode::SixPlayer` / `MAX_PLAYERS_6P`; board geometry extension point is `Types.hpp`
- Sound effects (capture, piece movement) are architecturally planned but not yet implemented

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Implement a full fledged ludo game featuring standard 4 player plus additional 6 player variant. The game must have all the standard ludo rules such as stacking and home entry after a kill/capture. It should offer an option to play game with a single die or pair. It will be 3d game written in C++ with Opengl and visually and mechanically it must be similar to windows' 7 chess titans but ludo.
> It is optional to implement debug tools ui in imgui for debug mode only. Use C++17 and onwards as C++ standard. Try to make it cross platform with preferred windows as main platform. It must follow OOP principles and modular design. It would be preferable if it followed MVC or other such design choice so that inner logic be decoupled from user interface or presentation. Game saving and loading are preferred. Now either four players are humans or 3 players are computer players. I will myself extend the game to be network playable but thats not your task so keep it modifiable and extendable.
> Game must be optimal and colorful with models for pieces and board alongwith their textures. Board should be rotatable like in Chess titans. And classes must be made for modules and components and standard design patterns and principles be followed. It must be primarily written in C++.

## Summary

- Rewrites BM25 tokenizer suffix rules as a language-agnostic `_normalize_token()` function — works for both Portuguese and English without hardcoding language-specific assumptions
- Portuguese-specific rules (ções, ões) simply never match English tokens; generic rules (ais→al, s→∅) work in both languages
- Updates README to fully document v1.1: semantic chunking, hybrid BM25+RRF, cross-encoder reranker, known limitations, updated configuration table, roadmap

## Changes

- `app/core/hybrid_search.py` — renamed `_stem_pt` to `_normalize_token`, rewrote docstring and comments to be language-neutral

## Known Limitations (documented in README)

Semantic search bridges natural synonyms well (falecer → morte, prazo de espera → carência) but struggles with unexpanded technical acronyms (IFPD). BM25 keyword search cannot match query terms to synonyms — hybrid search mitigates but does not eliminate this gap. Documented with concrete mitigations.

- [x] Synonym bridging validated: `falecer` and `prazo de espera` correctly resolved via semantic search

body:
After `mixed_audio.wav` is uploaded to S3, submit it to Transcribe and persist word-level timestamps for downstream use by the shorts pipeline.

## Audio handler (`nexus-audio/handler.py`)
- Added module-level `transcribe` client
- `_run_transcribe(run_id, s3_uri)`: starts job → polls every 5s up to 120s → on `COMPLETED`, parses raw Transcribe output and writes simplified format to `s3://nexus-outputs/{run_id}/audio/word_timestamps.json`; timeouts and all exceptions log a warning and continue (non-fatal)
- Called immediately after `mixed_audio.wav` upload

Output format:
```json
{"words": [{"word": "hello", "start": 0.0, "end": 0.5, "confidence": 0.99}]}
```

author: jeremymcs
body:
## Summary

Closes #140 — Makes GSD's auto-mode state machine extensible without forking core code.

Adds a **data-driven hook system** configured entirely through `preferences.md`:

- **Post-unit hooks** — Run after specific unit types complete (e.g., code review after `execute-task`, simplify pass, convention enforcement). Support retry loops with cycle limits.
- **Pre-dispatch hooks** — Intercept units before dispatch to modify prompts (inject context), skip units conditionally, or replace them entirely.
- **Hook state persistence** — Cycle counts survive crashes/restarts via `.gsd/hook-state.json`.
- **`/gsd hooks` command** — View configured hooks and their status.

### Configuration Example

```yaml
# .gsd/preferences.md
---
post_unit_hooks:
  - name: code-review
    after:
      - execute-task
    prompt: |
      Review the changes made in the last task.
      If critical issues found, write REVIEW-ISSUES.md.
      If acceptable, write REVIEW-PASS.md.
    max_cycles: 3
    artifact: REVIEW-PASS.md
    retry_on: REVIEW-ISSUES.md

  - name: simplify
    after:
      - execute-task
    prompt: Review code for unnecessary complexity and fix in-place.
    artifact: SIMPLIFY-RESULT.md

pre_dispatch_hooks:
  - name: inject-conventions
    before:
      - execute-task
    action: modify
    append: Follow project coding conventions and patterns.
---
```

### Use cases from issue discussion
| Contributor | Use Case | Configuration |
|------------|----------|---------------|
| @gtrak | Code review loop after task execution | `post_unit_hooks` with `retry_on` + `max_cycles: 3` |
| @frizynn | Simplify pass after code-producing stages | `post_unit_hooks` with `max_cycles: 1` |
| @FacuVCanale | Convention/pattern enforcement | `post_unit_hooks` or `pre_dispatch_hooks` with modify action |

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `post-unit-hooks.ts` | **New** — Hook engine (~400 lines): queue management, cycle tracking, pre-dispatch interception, state persistence, status reporting |
| `types.ts` | Added 7 interfaces: `PostUnitHookConfig`, `PreDispatchHookConfig`, `HookExecutionState`, `HookDispatchResult`, `PreDispatchResult`, `PersistedHookState`, `HookStatusEntry` |
| `preferences.ts` | Hook config parsing, validation (name/after/prompt required, max_cycles clamped 1-10, action-specific field requirements), merging (same-name override), resolve functions |
| `auto.ts` | Integration: post-unit hook dispatch in `handleAgentEnd()`, pre-dispatch hook interception in `dispatchNextUnit()`, state persistence on hook dispatch/start/stop, `hook/` prefix handling in progress display |
| `commands.ts` | `/gsd hooks` subcommand |

### Design decisions

1. **Zero behavior change when unconfigured** — Single empty-array check per dispatch, no impact on existing users
2. **Hooks are prompts, not code** — Same trust model as `custom_instructions` in preferences
3. **`hook/` unit type prefix** — Hook units naturally work with existing stuck detection, idempotency, and metrics
4. **Pre-dispatch skip uses `setImmediate` recursion** — Same pattern as existing idempotency skip to avoid tight recursion

### What this does NOT change
- State derivation (`state.ts`) — Untouched, no new phases
- Core dispatch logic — Hooks compose around it, not inside it
- Existing artifact verification — Hooks have their own artifact system

## Test plan

- [x] 72 new assertions across 2 test files (280/280 total pass)
- [x] Post-unit hook: artifact path resolution (task/slice/milestone levels)
- [x] Post-unit hook: hook-on-hook prevention
- [x] Post-unit hook: retry trigger consume/clear
- [x] Pre-dispatch hook: no-op when unconfigured
- [x] Pre-dispatch hook: bypass for hook unit types
- [x] State persistence: persist/restore/clear cycle counts
- [x] State persistence: handles missing and corrupt files
- [x] Hook status: formatting with no hooks configured
- [x] Preferences: validation rules for both hook types
- [x] Preferences: max_cycles clamping (1-10)
- [x] Preferences: same-name merge override behavior
- [x] Clean build with zero type errors

author: kwen2501
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.12.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #177473
* #177380
* __->__ #177463
* #177459
* #177472

Existing pattern: `find` + operator`[]`

Why `emplace` tends to be faster
Both patterns must probe the hash table at least once to decide whether the key exists. The difference is:
`find` + operator`[]` does two probes in the “not found” case:
probe 1 in `find(key)`
probe 2 in `operator[](key)` (it has to search again to find/insert)
`emplace(key, value)` does one probe and returns `{it, inserted}` in a single pass.

author: copilot
body:
Daily DAP scans top government pages and detects WCAG violations, but had no way to express *who* is excluded or *how many Americans* are affected each day. This PR ties axe findings to U.S. Census disability prevalence data and surfaces a per-disability "Americans excluded today" estimate in every daily report.

## New: Census disability data (`src/data/census-disability-stats.js`)
All 9 Section 508 FPC codes mapped to ACS 2022 prevalence rates, estimated U.S. populations, and per-category source citations (Census/CDC/NIDCD/NIH). Includes `vintage_year`, `next_review_date`, and helpers:
- `isCensusDataStale(date?)` — returns true if past review date
- `getFpcPrevalenceRates()` — plain `{code: rate}` map for existing pipeline use

## New: FPC exclusion calculator (`src/aggregation/fpc-exclusion.js`)
For each FPC category, sums `page_load_count` of successfully-scanned URLs whose axe findings map to that category (via existing `AXE_TO_FPC`), then multiplies by census prevalence:

```js
// color-contrast -> ['LV', 'WPC']; image-alt -> ['WV', 'WH']
// URL with 5M loads + color-contrast finding:
//   LV: 5,000,000 × 0.024 = 120,000 Americans excluded
//   WPC: 5,000,000 × 0.043 = 215,000 Americans excluded
```

## Updated: Daily report + HTML rendering
- `build-daily-report.js`: accepts `fpcExclusion` param, writes `fpc_exclusion` to report JSON
- `render-pages.js`: new `renderFpcExclusionSection()` — "Americans Excluded by Disability Today" table with FPC icons, U.S. population, page loads with barriers, and estimated excluded users
- `run-daily-scan.js`: wires in `computeFpcExclusion()` in aggregation stage; logs a staleness warning when census data is overdue
- `prevalence.yaml`: prevalence rate keys updated from generic names (`blindness`) to FPC codes (`WV`) to align with the mapping layer

## New: Annual census data check (`.github/workflows/check-census-data.yml`)
Runs January 2 each year. Calls `isCensusDataStale()` and opens a labelled GitHub issue with update instructions if the data is past its review date.

## Schema
`daily-report.schema.json` updated with the `fpc_exclusion` object shape (nullable, with per-FPC category entries).

💡 **What:** The optimization implemented
- Moved `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instantiation to the module level in Astro frontmatter for article list and detail pages.
- Reused a single `dateFormatter` instance instead of creating a new one on every `formatDate` call.

🎯 **Why:** The performance problem it solves
- `Intl` constructors are computationally expensive and memory-intensive.
- In list rendering (e.g., article blog), creating a new formatter per item causes unnecessary allocations and CPU overhead, especially as the number of articles grows.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
- A micro-benchmark showed that reusing the `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instance for 10,000 iterations is ~99.5% faster than re-instantiating it (Baseline: 3889.7ms, Optimized: 18.2ms).
- This change significantly reduces the overhead of date formatting during static site generation or server-side rendering for pages containing lists of articles.

author: toddr-bot
body:
## What
Fix EVP_PKEY_CTX and EVP_MD leaks in `verify()` when OpenSSL 3.x setup calls fail.

## Why
The `CHECK_OPEN_SSL` macro croaks immediately on failure. In `verify()`'s setup path (lines 1116-1130), if `EVP_PKEY_verify_init`, `EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_padding`, or `EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_signature_md` fails, the already-allocated `ctx` and `md` are never freed.

This completes the CHECK_OPEN_SSL → THROW cleanup campaign across all OpenSSL 3.x code paths in RSA.xs.

## How
Replace `CHECK_OPEN_SSL` with `THROW` for the setup calls, and add an `err:` label that frees both resources before croaking. Both `EVP_PKEY_CTX_free(NULL)` and `EVP_MD_free(NULL)` are documented no-ops, so the cleanup is safe regardless of which step fails.

## Testing
All 318 tests pass. The normal verify path is unchanged — only the error-path cleanup is new.

Creates a professional security audit report detailing a critical Arbitrary File Write vulnerability found in the `syscore` Aether upload handler (`syscore/src/server/aether.rs`). 

The vulnerability is due to a lack of sanitization of the multipart `filename` before it is joined with the storage directory path using `PathBuf::join`. Because `PathBuf::join` replaces the base path entirely when given an absolute path, an attacker can overwrite arbitrary files on the system.

This PR adds:
- `SECURITY_ISSUE.md`: The complete vulnerability report using the required GitHub Issue format.
- `.jules/sentinel.md`: The architectural findings and vulnerability pattern journal entry.

As per Sentinel's mandate, no application code was modified.

author: cardosaum
body:
Replaces thiserror with snafu on `FrankClawError`. Every error now carries the file:line:column where it was created.

## Error construction

Before:
```rust
Err(FrankClawError::Channel { channel: id, msg: format!("timeout") })
```

After:
```rust
ChannelSnafu { channel: id, msg: "timeout" }.fail()
```

The snafu context selector captures the caller location automatically via `#[track_caller]`.

## What changed

- `error.rs` rewritten: 28 variants with `#[snafu(display(...))]` + implicit `Location` field
- `FrankClawError::location()` returns the creation site for any error
- `channel_err()` on `ChannelPlugin` uses `#[track_caller]` to forward location
- ~370 construction sites migrated across 44 files in all 13 crates
- Crypto variant uses `#[snafu(context(false))]` for automatic `From` impl

## Tests

Single `error_cases()` table covers all 28 variants. Three parameterized rstest tests verify display message, status code, and retryability — no duplication. Guard test catches missing coverage when new variants are added. Location tests verify file and line capture at the actual call site.

90 error-specific tests, 774 total, all pass.
